plan.title: Implement planOrder with order, stages and typed planning errors
plan.description: Implement planOrder(tasks: TaskSpec[]) => {order, stages} per SPEC.md section 2. Detect duplicate ids, unknown dependencies, cycles and throw typed errors extending TaskPlanError (e.g. DuplicateTaskError, UnknownDependencyError, CycleError) with expected properties. Use Kahn/topological sort for deterministic order and level-based stages for parallel execution. Export from src/index.ts and add JSDoc API comments.
acceptance: planOrder returns correct topological order and stages for linear, diamond and independent graphs
Duplicate id throws typed error with duplicate id info
Unknown dependency throws typed error with taskId and dep info
Cycle throws typed CycleError with cycle path
tsc passes and planner check group passes
plan.reason: Core algorithm with cycle detection and typed error design needs strong reasoning.
plan.escalate_if: Spec ambiguity on tie-breaking or cycle reporting makes tests fail.

plan.title: Add plan CLI command with output formats and exit codes
plan.description: Add CLI entry (src/cli.ts) implementing `plan` command per SPEC.md section 3: read tasks JSON/file/stdin, call planOrder, support --format human/json, --stages flag, print order/stages, handle planning errors with typed messages and exit codes 0/1/2. Wire via npx/ts-node invocation expected by tests.
acceptance: plan CLI outputs order as JSON and human format correctly
CLI maps duplicate/unknown/cycle errors to stderr messages and non-zero exit codes per spec
CLI invalid JSON input handled per spec
plan.reason: Requires correct I/O handling, format branching and error-to-exit-code mapping.
plan.escalate_if: CLI test harness invocation differs from assumed entry point.

plan.title: Add runnable example, README Planning section, CHANGELOG and API comments
plan.description: Create examples/basic.ts runnable demo of planOrder and verify its output per SPEC.md section 4. Add README.md Planning section documenting usage/order/stages/errors and CLI examples. Add CHANGELOG.md entry for new feature. Ensure public APIs have JSDoc comments.
acceptance: examples/basic.ts runs with ts-node/tsx and prints expected order/stages output
README contains Planning section with planOrder and plan CLI usage
CHANGELOG has entry for planOrder feature under Unreleased/appropriate version
API comments present for planOrder and error types
plan.reason: Docs and example wiring is mechanical once planner/CLI are stable.
plan.escalate_if: Example output expectation mismatches actual deterministic order.

findings.evidence: The --stages flag is parsed but never controls output: human-format always prints stages and ignores stagesFlag, making the flag a no-op.
findings.suggested_check: Run the CLI in human format without --stages on a 2-stage graph and verify only 'Order:' is printed; with --stages verify 'Stage 1:' appears, to confirm flag gating.

findings.evidence: USAGE documents --json/shorthand file arg only and omits --format human/json and --stages defined by SPEC 3; also message printed for all input/flag errors may not match SPEC phrasing.
findings.suggested_check: Compare CLI --help/usage output against SPEC.md section 3 example invocations ( --format, --stages, stdin via -) .

findings.evidence: Zero positional args is always treated as usage error; SPEC says plan reads file/json/stdin. If SPEC expects implicit stdin when no file is given, piped JSON would be rejected.
findings.suggested_check: Pipe JSON to `node src/cli.ts plan` with no file arg (or with inherited stdin) and check whether it plans vs exits 2; also test explicit '-' stdin case.

findings.snippet:
if (jsonMode) {
      const out = JSON.stringify({ order: result.order, stages: result.stages });
findings.evidence: JSON output always includes both order and stages regardless of --stages. If SPEC expects --stages to gate stages in JSON as well, unconditional stages field violates it.
findings.suggested_check: Compare `plan file.json --format json` vs `plan file.json --format json --stages` JSON keys against SPEC expected output.
